what_it_does: In GPU-heavy computer systems, the uncore components (memory, cache, and interconnect hardware) typically stay at maximum frequency even when they're not being fully used, wasting power. This work develops MAGUS, a runtime system that monitors memory access patterns to predict how intensive the workload is, detects when the system switches between different execution phases, and scales the uncore frequency up or down accordingly while maintaining smooth transitions. The system integrates with vendor power management tools and requires no changes from users.
